reduck/chatgpt.com/ask [write] — Open a new ChatGPT chat, send one question, wait for the answer to finish (up to 3 min), and return what the model answered, the sources it cited, the searches it ran, and what ChatGPT itself reports about how it searched.

Answers come back as a list, not one string. ChatGPT sometimes serves a paired-response variant that answers the same question twice and asks which reply you prefer; that returns two entries and neither is more official than the other. Read the length before reading answers[0]. Text is as rendered, so a citation chip appears inline as its publisher's name and mathematical notation linearizes lossily.

`references` is every page the answer actually cited — publisher, title and url, deduplicated and in the order the answer surfaced them. `sources` is the larger pool the searches put in front of the model. An empty `references` means that reply did not search, which is a fact about the reply rather than a failure — the same question searches on one run and not the next, so repeat a question before concluding anything from it.

`webSearchQueries` is what ChatGPT typed into its search, in order. `searches` groups those queries by round with the results each round returned. `calls` gives each search call on its own, as ChatGPT numbers it, with every result's type (web, reddit, news, academia…), position, snippet and date. One call often runs several queries and returns one list for all of them, so a result's position is in that list, not the rank for a single query.

`searchContext` is what ChatGPT's server says about the turn: the name of its internal search tool, the region that answered, a label for the kind of turn, and the location the answer was made for when it gives one. ChatGPT no longer sends it to a signed-in page, so it is empty there. None of this names an outside search engine: ChatGPT does not tell the page which index answered, which query returned which result, or which arguments a call used.

Signed in, every other field is filled, and the account's saved memory biases the answer toward whatever you discussed with it before. Signed out, ChatGPT has been seen serving two different applications: one sends `webSearchQueries` and `searchContext`, the other (it opens a /uc/ chat) sends only the cited `references`, so both come back empty there even when the reply searched. `searches`, `sources`, `calls`, `answer` and `stopReason` are signed-in only.
